learning_outcomes.text: Identify key business activities and functions, and understand their relationship to resources and outcomes.
Grasp the elements of feasibility, the interplay between costs, revenues, and volume, and the concept of the break-even point.
Understand the fundamentals of management systems, with a specific focus on quality, non-conformity, and performance evaluation.
Comprehend the essential structure of financial statements, key performance indicators, and various organizational models.
Describe business processes, functions, tasks, and responsibilities.
Perform basic break-even analyses and interpret key line items in financial statements.
Analyze business performance indicators and identify quality-related aspects within a process, product, or service.
Evaluate the feasibility of an initiative based on available data.
Interpret economic, asset-related, and financial information.
Identify critical quality-related issues and compare the characteristics of different organizational models.
Describe a business, its processes, and its functions using appropriate professional terminology.
Present the results of simple economic analyses and comment on financial statement information and aspects of quality management.
Connect organization, management, resources, and economic outcomes.
Apply the knowledge acquired to business examples and use it to independently explore the course topics further.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the enterprise: The enterprise, its objectives, and key business activities; the relationship between organization, resources, and economic results. Economic and organizational terminology.

Feasibility elements of business initiatives: Preliminary analysis of the market, potential customers, and alternatives; factors influencing location choice. Relationship between costs, revenues, and activity volumes; break-even analysis. Main types of investment and introduction to business performance indicators.

Process-based organization and management systems: Business processes, responsibilities, and inter-functional coordination. Purpose and structure of a management system: goal setting, activity planning, results monitoring, and improvement. Introduction to management system standards, with examples regarding quality, the environment, and information security. In-depth look at quality management systems: customer requirements, product/service and process quality, non-conformity management and performance evaluation, quality-to-price ratio, and performance trends.

Elements of business economics and financial statement analysis: Classification of business costs; purpose, general principles, and structure of the annual financial statements. Introduction to the balance sheet and the income statement; interpretation of key items and basic reclassification of the income statement. Economic, asset-based, and financial indicators. The cash flow statement, cash flows, and the distinction between economic results and cash availability.

Organizational structures and people: Business functions and the distribution of tasks and responsibilities; main organizational structure models. The individual within the organization and the fundamentals of human resource management; vertical and horizontal coordination and integration. Examples also drawn from companies developing IT products and services.
assessment_rules: The oral examination consists of three questions, each scored from 0 to 10. The final grade (out of 30) is the sum of these scores. A minimum grade of 18/30 is required to pass. Attending students may take two midterm tests; if both are taken and the arithmetic mean of their scores (out of 30) is at least 18/30, the oral examination is optional.
